critique.good: 五个月份列宽相近，表头和销量均保持单行；各行等高，便于横向追踪和纵向比较。门店列在保证数值完整的前提下取得了较大宽度。
critique.problems: 门店名称仍被拆成不理想的两行，例如“南京新／街口店”和“合肥淮／河路店”，商圈名称难以一眼识别。
critique.cause: 门店列为81px，扣除21px后仅有60px内容宽度；五个月份列已经接近容纳最长数值所需的最小宽度。

critique.good: 五个月份列均为56px，数字区域节奏整齐，表头和数值都保持单行；各行高度一致。
critique.problems: 门店名称的断行仍拆开了商圈名称，视觉效果与r0A几乎相同。
critique.cause: 门店列为79px，内容宽度只有58px；为月份列取得完全相等的宽度，门店列比r0A少了2px。

critique.good: 月份列等宽，表头和销量均完整显示，数字区域宽松且便于纵向比较。
critique.problems: 门店名称仍在商圈内部断行；月份列增加的空白没有改善行高或数值可读性，却进一步压缩了作为行标识的门店列。
critique.cause: 门店列缩至69px，扣除边框和内边距后只有48px内容宽度；每个月份列增至58px，超出保持数值单行所需。

r0A.idea: 优先给门店名称四个汉字的空间，月份列按各自内容的最小单行宽度分配，保住数字并改善行标识。

r0B.idea: 让五个月份列等宽并恰好容纳最长数字，其余宽度留给门店名称，在行标识和整齐的数字区之间取得平衡。

r0C.idea: 给五个月份列更多且相等的数字留白，以门店名称更频繁地在地名中间换行作为代价。

contrast.idea: The wider store column would keep more names intact, but each month would have only 29px for text. Four-digit sales figures would split, making comparisons across the five months much harder.

reviewerFeedback:
another layout was rated acceptable: Column 1 gets about 72px, so all store names break 3+2 (上海徐/汇店, 南京新/街口店), cutting place names in half; the resulting two-line blocks are even and the five month columns stay equal and comfortably wide, so numbers scan cleanly, but the row headers are the weak point. | your previous preferred design was rated acceptable: Effectively the same as A: identical 3+2 wrapping of store names (杭州西/湖店, 苏州观/前店), even two-line row blocks and even month columns; nothing broken, but row identity is split mid-place-name, which slows reading down the header column. | another layout was rated acceptable: Same 3+2 name wrap as A and B; month columns look evenly proportioned and the numeric grid reads as a clean block, yet the header column still chops 徐汇, 西湖 and 新街口, so the row labels lose a little integrity. | another layout was rated good: The wider header column lets each name put city+district on line one (上海徐汇, 南京新街, 合肥淮河) and isolates the generic suffix 店 on line two, so the distinguishing part stays intact and the lone 店 forms a consistent vertical rhythm; the cost is slightly squeezed month columns (numbers sit closer to the rules) and a stranded single character per row, but the table scans better down the row headers. | another layout was rated poor: The header column is so narrow that names break into three lines (上海/徐汇/店, 南京/新街/口店), producing very tall, airy rows; the whole table becomes a ladder of text with the month figures floating far apart, breaking row cohesion and vertical comparison between months. | another layout was rated acceptable: Same 3+2 split as A/B/C with balanced month columns; readable and consistent, but the row-header breaks fall inside place names (宁波天/一店, 合肥淮/河路店), which is the weakest aspect of an otherwise tidy grid.
another layout was rated poor: 门店 column is only about three characters wide, so every store name splits mid-word (上海徐/汇店, 杭州西/湖店, 苏州观/前店, 宁波天/一店), breaking the branch names readers scan by. The month columns still have spare room that should have gone to column 1. | another layout was rated good: Best balance of the compact layouts: the wider row-header column keeps most branch names intact (上海徐汇/店, 杭州西湖/店), leaving only the trailing 店 orphaned, while all four-digit figures still sit on one line. A few bad splits remain (南京新街/口店), but the table stays compact and scannable. | another layout was rated poor: Same failure as A: three-character header column cuts through branch names (徐/汇, 西/湖, 观/前, 天/一), so row identity is fragmented while the month columns carry unnecessary slack. | another layout was rated poor: Row headers again wrap at three characters, splitting 徐汇, 西湖, 观前 and 天一 across lines; the month columns are wider than the numbers require, so the space is misallocated. | your previous preferred design was rated poor: Visually the same compromise as A/C/D: row labels break inside branch names and the numeric columns keep extra width that column 1 needs more. | another layout was rated acceptable: Two-character breaks give a readable city/branch rhythm (上海/徐汇/店, 苏州/观前/店), but 新街口 and 淮河路 still split badly (口店, 路店), and every row becomes three lines tall. The month columns are clearly over-wide for four-digit numbers, wasting width that could have kept column 1 to two or three clean lines.

understanding.purpose: 展示华东区各门店2024年1—5月的月度销量，便于比较门店和月份。
understanding.reading: 读者会先沿门店列定位分店，再横向查看其月度变化；也会纵向比较同一月份各店销量。每行应保持紧凑，让门店名称与五个数值读作一个整体。
groups: 1月至5月是同类、连续的时间列，应保持相近宽度，形成便于比较的数字区域。
门店列是行标识，需要足够空间呈现区分各分店的地名。
keep_intact: 每个销量数值应保持在一行。
尽可能保持城市和商圈等有辨识度的名称完整。
may_wrap: 门店名称可换成两行；优先将通用后缀“店”放在第二行，避免把商圈名称拆开。
名称已经换成两行时，行高可以容纳第二行，无需再为单字后缀增加额外高度。

bad.why: The wider store column would keep more names intact, but each month would have only 29px for text. Four-digit sales figures would split, making comparisons across the five months much harder.

contrast.why: The wider store column would keep more names intact, but each month would have only 29px for text. Four-digit sales figures would split, making comparisons across the five months much harder.

final.rationale: r0B gives the five equivalent month columns equal widths while keeping every sales figure on one line. The store names wrap to two lines, but the resulting rows remain consistent and easy to scan across. r0A is nearly as good, though its month widths vary slightly; r0C gives the month columns more space without reducing the wrapping of store names.

general: Columns with the same role benefit from a consistent rhythm when their contents have similar width requirements.
Keeping values intact supports comparison across a row; a wrapped row label can be an acceptable use of space.
specific: All five monthly columns need roughly 55–56px to accommodate their widest values with the fixed padding and borders.
Within the available width, none of these candidates can keep every store name on one line while also preserving intact monthly figures.

final.tradeoffs: A designer could prefer r0A's slightly wider store column or r0C's more generous spacing around the monthly values. Both retain the same row heights and intact figures.
final.uncertain: The ranges describe small coordinated adjustments around r0B, not independent widths that can all be maximized at once: the total must remain at most 359px, and each month's values must still fit. The exact visual equivalence of adjustments within those limits depends on the rendered result.

A.why: All sales figures stay intact, and the month columns have a steady rhythm. Store names wrap over two lines, making them slower to scan.

B.why: The figures remain intact and the month columns are nearly equal. Every store name wraps over two lines.

C.why: The month columns are evenly proportioned and the figures stay intact. Store names wrap over two lines, but the rows remain easy to follow.

D.why: The wider store column keeps more of each name together while all figures remain intact. Several names leave a short final line, and the month columns remain balanced.

E.why: Store names break across three lines, leaving tall rows with large empty areas beside the figures and making the names harder to scan.

F.why: Several four-digit sales figures break across lines, disrupting comparisons and making the values difficult to read.

reviews.unsure: B, C and D are close: D gives store names slightly more room, while C has slightly more even month columns.

A.why: The five month columns are evenly balanced and every sales figure stays intact. Store names wrap to two lines, but their line breaks are reasonably balanced and the rows remain easy to scan.

B.why: The figures remain intact and the month columns are balanced, but several store names leave a lone character on the second line, weakening the row labels.

C.why: The figures stay intact and the month columns have a consistent rhythm. The narrower store column wraps every name, making the labels slightly more cramped.

D.why: Several four-digit sales figures split across lines, making values difficult to read and compare across months. The wider store column does not compensate for that loss.

E.why: The month columns are balanced, all figures stay intact, and the store names wrap into reasonably balanced two-line labels.

F.why: The store column is so narrow that names break into three lines, making row identification slow and producing tall, sparse rows despite intact figures.

reviews.unsure: A and E appear very close; their small width difference is difficult to judge precisely from the images.
